chapter: Honors, Gibson and Dorsey late years
title: First wife leaves with their son
summary: On Christmas Day 1947 Charlie Shavers tells Leeman that his first wife has emptied their Maine house and left with their son, and Shavers looks out for him.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: first place, we opened Christmas Day, and my Christmas present, Charlie picked me up at the dressing room which we shared, and informed me that my wife, my first wife, had taken my son and left me. She was in Maine, living in my home, which I love so dearly, and had built -- and she cleaned the house out and took everything -- all the furniture and was gone. But she left a sofa, I guess it had something to do with the law, you had to leave something for someone to lay down on, to be within the law. So she left me a sectional divan and my two shotguns in front of the fireplace, and that's all she left.

However, to continue -- I was in a pretty bad state of mind, and that's when Charlie Shavers and I became closer and closer friends. Charlie Shavers looked out for me, because I used to come in and get down on my hands and knees to have a water glass full of booze before the first show, to stop the shakes and I could go on. That's just a byline ...
